reject_comment.r1: Please note that the Materials Cloud Archive is dedicated to computational materials science, and it appears that your submission may fall outside this scope. We recommend depositing your data on https://zenodo.org instead. If you believe your work is relevant to computational materials science and would like to clarify how it fits within this domain, please don’t hesitate to contact us. Adding a more detailed description and a reference link might help us to better understand the topic of your work. Otherwise, I will proceed with declining your request to publish.
reject_comment.r2: Please note that the Materials Cloud Archive is dedicated to computational materials science, and it appears that your submission may primarily consist of experimental work. If you believe your work is relevant to computational materials science and would like to clarify how it fits within this domain, please don’t hesitate to contact us. Otherwise, I will proceed with declining your request to publish.
reject_comment.r3: Thank you for your submission to the Materials Cloud Archive repository. After careful consideration, we regret to inform you that we are unable to accept the record for publication, as it does not align with the scope of the repository that is computational materials science. We appreciate your interest and suggest that you consider submitting your work to a more general purpose repository such as Zenodo (https://zenodo.org), which may be better suited for the content of your record. Thank you for your understanding.
reject_comment.r4: Before reviewing your submission, we would like to know whether this study is mainly experimental or if it also includes some computational work. The Materials Cloud Archive is dedicated to computational materials science, and it appears that your submission may fall outside this scope. Could you clarify ?

files.f1: - Please add a file named files_description.md or README.md/.txt that lists each filename along with a brief description of its contents. You can find examples of these files in other published records (Example: https://archive.materialscloud.org/record/2025.98).
files.f2: - We would like to maintain a consistent file format for the files_description.md file across all records we publish. Could you please rename the file describing the contents to files_description.md? You can download an example from another published record (e.g., https://archive.materialscloud.org/record/2025.104). Please keep the same syntax, using ** to make filenames appear in bold, and modify it accordingly to reflect the correct filenames and their descriptions.
files.f3: - Please remove the sentence 'This file is automatically generated. It contains the descriptions of each uploaded file as provided by the user.' from the file files_description.md. This sentence was automatically added to records during the migration of the Archive to a new version in June 2025. You do not need to include it in your files_description.md file.
files.f4: - Please add a README.md/.txt file or a files_description.md file that provides detailed information about the structure and content of the archive file/s.
files.f5: - Please add a file named files_description.md that lists each filename along with a brief description of its contents. It contains the descriptions of each uploaded file as provided by the user.'
files.f7: - The file format is not open. To ensure accessibility and long-term usability, please replace the file with an open and supported alternative, such as .zip or .tar.zip.
files.f8: - Please add a file extension (.txt or .md) to the README file so that it can be opened correctly in Preview.

title.t1: - Please revise the title to use lowercase letters, except for the first word.
title.t3: - Please revise the title so that it follows the format of a journal paper title.

Resource type.rt1: - You selected 'Software' as the resource type, although you uploaded dataset files. Could you please explain your choice, or select 'Dataset' instead?

description.d1: - There is a misspell in the description
description.d2: - Could you move the sentence 'This dataset contains ...' at the end of the description or place it in a README.txt or files_description.md file ?
description.d3: - The description should clarify the topic and purpose of the work, and briefly explain the contents of the dataset. It should be in the format of an abstract for a journal paper.
description.d4: - You have some return characters in the description that cause the text to be aligned to the left. Could you please remove those characters?
description.d5: - Could you move the current description in a README.txt file ?
description.d7: - Please start the description with a capital letter.
description.d8: - Please add a full stop at the end of the description.
description.d9: - Please revise the description so that it resembles the abstract of a journal article.

authors.a1: - Are you the sole author of this work? If not, please add the names of all co-authors.

affiliations.af1: - Please remove the numbers (e.g., 1., 2.) in front of the institute/university names. The numbering is automatically generated. You can preview how the record will appear by clicking on Preview and then on Show affiliations.
affiliations.af2: - Please add the full address for each affiliation. Affiliations should include the name of the institute, faculty, or department; the name of the university or research center; and the location. For example: Theory and Simulation of Materials (THEOS), École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), CH-1015 Lausanne, Switzerland. Alternatively, you can start typing the name of the affiliation and select it from the dropdown menu. This will register the affiliation using its ROR ID (see https://ror.org). You can preview how the record will appear by clicking on Preview and then on Show affiliations.
affiliations.af3: - Please add the affiliation of each author.

references.ref1: - Since your paper is not yet published, please remove the DOI link, as the link does not currently resolve. Instead, add a comment such as "Submitted to The Journal of Chemical Physics.". Once your paper is published, you will be able to update the reference and include the DOI.
references.ref2: - Please add the full journal reference, including the authors, title and reference number if available. If the article has not yet been published, include a comment such as 'Submitted'. If it has been published, please provide a link to the journal (DOI or URL).
references.ref3: - The DOI link is incorrect. Please correct it and use only the last part of the URL, do not include 'https://doi.org/'. If the DOI link does not resolve because the paper is not yet published, please remove the link from the record. Once this record is published, you will still be able to update the references and add the DOI link when your paper is published.
references.ref4: - Please correct the DOI link, use only the last part of the URL with the DOI, do not include 'https://doi.org/'.
references.ref5: - If your paper has been submitted or is not yet submitted, please add the list of authors, the title, and the name of the journal you plan to submit it to. Include a comment such as 'Submitted' or 'To be submitted' (see, for example: https://archive.materialscloud.org/record/2025.121).
references.ref6: - If the paper is published, please add a link to the reference. You may provide either a URL or a DOI.
references.ref7: - Could you please provide a link (DOI or URL) to the preprint? Once your paper is published, you will be able to update the reference.

licenses.l1: - Please note that the license addendum from the previous version is not automatically included in this version. If you wish to add it, create a file named license_addendum.txt and include the sentence used in the previous version.

keywords.k1: - Add minimum 3 keywords. Keywords should be added one at a time in the upload form. Press 'Enter' after typing each keyword.
